### Parts Tariffs Need a System First [...] The 10% universal tariff that starts on April 5 will apply to nearly all imported goods, including vehicles and vehicle components. This serves as a baseline rate across countries.
 The additional country- and product-specific tariffs that go into effect April 9 concern vehicles and parts from countries with large trade deficits with the U.S. —such as Germany, Japan, South Korea, and China. These rates may rise to 25% or higher.

Ram, as with other Stellantis brands, is offering employee pricing to all customers on eligible models through June 30.

### Pricing impact

Employee pricing is available for eligible Ram models through June 30.

### Production impact

The Hemi V8 engine will return to Ram’s light-duty pickup lineup for the 2026 model year.

### Manufacturer response

Rivian has not announced any official response to the tariffs.

### Pricing impact [...] Audi has halted all imports to the U.S. and is holding incoming inventory at port in response to new tariffs. While vehicles imported before the tariffs will keep prior pricing, future imports are expected to reflect added costs through increased destination fees.

### Pricing impact

Audi has announced price increases for most of its 2026 models, ranging from $800 to $4,100. The largest increases will affect premium models, including the A8 and RS 7.

### Production impact [...] Tesla has expressed concerns about the impact of the recent 25% U.S. tariffs on imported vehicles and auto parts. In a letter dated March 11, 2025, Tesla informed the Trump administration that these tariffs could increase production costs for vehicles manufactured in the U.S. The company emphasized its efforts to localize the supply chain but acknowledged continued reliance on global parts sourcing.

### How Will Tariffs Impact the Prices of Cars?

Prices for new cars could increase by as much as $6,000 per vehicle on models under $40,000. This significant hike is due to the added cost of importing vehicles and parts, which manufacturers will likely pass on to consumers. As a result, both new and used car markets will be affected, with potential ripple effects on financing and insurance costs.
